title: Orthonormal Fourier system
statement: Let $\Omega$ and $\iota$ be finite sets. A complex Fourier system on these sets consists of a probability mass function $\mu$ on $\Omega$ that assigns positive mass to every point, a basis $(\phi_i)_{i\in\iota}$ of the complex vector space of functions on $\Omega$, and a distinguished index $i_0\in\iota$. The distinguished basis function is constant one, and the basis is orthonormal for the inner product weighted by $\mu$: $\sum_{x\in\Omega}\mu(x)\overline{\phi_i(x)}\phi_j(x)=1$ when $i=j$ and $0$ otherwise.
hypotheses_covered: $\mu$ is a probability mass function on $\Omega$
Every point of $\Omega$ has positive mass
$(\phi_i)_{i\in\iota}$ is a basis of the complex-valued functions on $\Omega$
The distinguished basis function is constant one
The basis is orthonormal for the $\mu$-weighted inner product
